members.summary: How `lucid.peft.get_peft_model` adapts a model with prompt tuning.
members.extended:
Prompt tuning (Lester et al., 2021, [arXiv:2104.08691](https://arxiv.org/abs/2104.08691)) freezes the model and
learns `num_virtual_tokens` embedding vectors that are put in front of
the input embeddings: the only trained parameters are
`num_virtual_tokens * token_dim` numbers, and a task is a file of that size.
An encoder-decoder model gets them in front of the encoder's input.

Field names, their order, defaults and `adapter_config.json` are the reference adapter
library's.

parameters.name: prompt_tuning_init
parameters.description:
`"RANDOM"` keeps the embedding table's initialisation; `"SAMPLE_VOCAB"`
starts from the embeddings of random vocabulary tokens; `"TEXT"`
starts from those of `prompt_tuning_init_text`'s tokens (cut or
repeated to `num_virtual_tokens`).

parameters.name: prompt_tuning_init_text
parameters.description: The text `"TEXT"` starts from; required then.

parameters.name: tokenizer_name_or_path
parameters.description: Names the tokenizer that turns that text into ids; required for `"TEXT"`.

parameters.name: tokenizer_kwargs
parameters.description: Keyword arguments for loading that tokenizer; only with `"TEXT"`.

raises.description: A field holds a value of the wrong type.
`"TEXT"` without its text or tokenizer, or `tokenizer_kwargs` without `"TEXT"`.

examples:
>>> from lucid.peft import PromptTuningConfig
>>> config = PromptTuningConfig(num_virtual_tokens=8, task_type="CAUSAL_LM")
>>> config.peft_type, config.prompt_tuning_init
(<PeftType.PROMPT_TUNING: 'PROMPT_TUNING'>, <PromptTuningInit.RANDOM: 'RANDOM'>)
>>> PromptTuningConfig.from_dict(config.to_dict()) == config
True

methods.summary: Build the virtual-token embedding.
methods.extended:
Its rows start from text, from sampled vocabulary rows or at random, as
`config.prompt_tuning_init` says; `word_embeddings` is the model's token table and
`tokenizer` turns `prompt_tuning_init_text` into ids.

methods.name: from_config
methods.summary: The embedding for `config`, started from `word_embeddings`.

methods.name: stores_prompt
methods.summary: Always `True`: the embedding's rows are the prompt.

methods.name: forward
methods.summary: Embeddings of the virtual-token ids: `(*, ...)` ids to `(*, ..., token_dim)`.

methods.name: per_task
methods.summary: Whether the prompt depends on the task each batch row belongs to (`task_ids`).

methods.name: stored
methods.summary: The tensors an adapter file holds, by the encoder's own key and the file's: the prompt always, and whatever else the method keeps beside it.

methods.name: num_embeddings
methods.summary: How many virtual tokens the encoder produces.

methods.name: indices
methods.summary: The virtual-token ids `(1, num_embeddings)` the encoder is called with.

methods.name: prompts
methods.summary: The prompt of each of `batch` rows: `(batch, num_embeddings, width)`.
methods.extended:
`tasks` is the task of each row, which a `per_task` encoder needs and the others
do not read.

methods.name: prompt_embeddings
methods.summary: The prompt as an adapter file stores it: `(rows, width)`, one row per virtual token.
methods.extended: A per-task encoder's is the shared prompt its tasks scale, which is what the file holds.

members.summary: The prompt of prompt tuning: one learned embedding per virtual token.

parameters.name: config
parameters.description:
Sizes (`num_virtual_tokens`, `num_transformer_submodules` and
`token_dim` set) and the initialisation.

parameters.name: word_embeddings
parameters.description:
The model's token table, which `"SAMPLE_VOCAB"` and `"TEXT"`
copy rows of.

parameters.name: tokenizer
parameters.description:
Turns `prompt_tuning_init_text` into ids for `"TEXT"`.  Left out, the
tokenizer `config.tokenizer_name_or_path` names is resolved (a registered
name, built from `config.tokenizer_kwargs`, or a directory).

raises.description:
`"TEXT"` initialisation whose tokenizer cannot be resolved or tokenizes the text
to nothing.

examples:
>>> import lucid
>>> import lucid.nn as nn
>>> from lucid.peft import PromptTuningConfig
>>> from lucid.peft.tuners.prompt_tuning import PromptEmbedding
>>> config = PromptTuningConfig(num_virtual_tokens=3, token_dim=8, num_transformer_submodules=1)
>>> PromptEmbedding(config, nn.Embedding(10, 8))(lucid.arange(3).long()).shape
(3, 8)

methods.name: forward

methods.extended: The prompt is put in by hooks on the model's own call, so nothing is applied here.

methods.name: get_model_config
methods.summary: `model`'s config as a dict, whatever it is held as.
methods.extended:
A config with a `to_dict` method is converted by it, a dataclass by `asdict`, a
mapping is copied.  A model with no `config` (or one that is `None`) has the
reference's stand-in, `{"model_type": "custom"}`, which is what the default target
modules and the prompt geometry read for a model of no known type.

parameters.name: model
parameters.description: The model to read the config of.

returns.description: The config's entries; a new dict, whose changes do not reach the model.

raises.description: `model.config` is none of a mapping, a dataclass or an object with `to_dict`.

examples:
>>> import lucid.nn as nn
>>> from lucid.peft import LoraModel
>>> LoraModel.get_model_config(nn.Linear(2, 2))
{'model_type': 'custom'}

members.summary: The tuner of prompt tuning: a `PromptEmbedding` per adapter, put in front of the input.

summary: `lucid.peft.tuners.prompt_tuning` — prompt tuning: learned embeddings in front of the input.
extended:
Prompt tuning (Lester et al., 2021, [arXiv:2104.08691](https://arxiv.org/abs/2104.08691)) freezes the model and learns
`num_virtual_tokens` embedding vectors that are put in front of the input embeddings.  The only
trained parameters are `num_virtual_tokens * token_dim` numbers, so a task is a file of that size.
The prompt starts from text, from sampled vocabulary rows or at random (`PromptTuningInit`).
Pick it for the smallest per-task files on a large model; it adds no layer, and trains one prompt at
a time.

The prompt is applied by hooks on the model's own call.  Here: `PromptEmbedding` (what is
learned) and `PromptTuningModel` (the tuner).  `PromptTuningConfig` and `PromptTuningInit` are
here too and exported from `lucid.peft`.
citation: Lester, Brian, et al. "The Power of Scale for Parameter-Efficient Prompt Tuning." [arXiv:2104.08691](https://arxiv.org/abs/2104.08691), 2021.
theory:
Prompt tuning (Lester et al., 2021, [arXiv:2104.08691](https://arxiv.org/abs/2104.08691)) freezes the model and
learns `num_virtual_tokens` embedding vectors that are put in front of
the input embeddings: the only trained parameters are
`num_virtual_tokens * token_dim` numbers, and a task is a file of that size.
An encoder-decoder model gets them in front of the encoder's input.
